sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.content: Live review on 2026-08-24 confirmed the W3C recommendation and its Entity, Activity, Agent, attribution, association, and delegation relations. This supports provenance vocabulary, not a complete application authorization model.

verifier_provenance.scope_note: Canonical technical standard; promoted only for the scoped provenance claims.

sources.title: A Truth Maintenance System
sources.content: Publisher metadata and the author's publication archive identify Jon Doyle, Artificial Intelligence 12(3), 231-272, November 1979. The paper records reasons for beliefs and revises beliefs when assumptions are contradicted.

verifier_provenance.correction_note: The candidate DOI 10.1016/0004-3702(79)90020-9 was rejected as a near-miss; canonical DOI is 10.1016/0004-3702(79)90008-0. The error is preserved here rather than overwritten in the historical registry.

sources.title: On the Acceptability of Arguments and its Fundamental Role in Nonmonotonic Reasoning, Logic Programming and n-Person Games
sources.content: Publisher and DBLP metadata identify Phan Minh Dung, Artificial Intelligence 77(2), 1995. The article develops an abstract theory centered on argument acceptability and relates it to nonmonotonic reasoning and logic programming.

verifier_provenance.scope_note: Independent author/canonical work from F16 despite a shared journal publisher.

sources.title: Argument-Based Extended Logic Programming with Defeasible Priorities
sources.content: Author and bibliographic records identify Henry Prakken and Giovanni Sartor, Journal of Applied Non-Classical Logics 7(1), 25-75, 1997. It presents defeasible argumentation with priorities and a dialectical proof theory.

verifier_provenance.correction_note: The earlier Journal of Logic and Computation / 10.1093/logcom/7.1.25 attribution was rejected; the preserved canonical record is Journal of Applied Non-Classical Logics with DOI 10.1080/11663081.1997.10510900.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025
sources.content: The official OWASP archive identifies the 2025 LLM application risk list, including prompt injection, supply-chain risks, improper output handling, and excessive agency. It is retained as a dated baseline rather than described as the latest edition.

verifier_provenance.scope_note: Historical 2025 baseline; not labeled current after the 2026 publication.

sources.title: Agentic AI Threats and Mitigations
sources.content: The official OWASP page, published 2025-02-17, presents a threat-model-based reference for emerging agentic AI risks and mitigations. It shares a publisher group with I1 and Z13 and therefore cannot multiply independence by itself.

verifier_provenance.scope_note: Corroborates the OWASP family but counts as the same independence group as I1 and Z13.

sources.title: in-toto
sources.content: The official project page describes an open framework that records which supply-chain steps were performed, by whom, and in what order, and identifies in-toto as a CNCF graduated project.

verifier_provenance.scope_note: Independent provenance/supply-chain group from W3C and OWASP.

sources.title: Firewall for AI
sources.content: Cloudflare's 2024-03-04 article describes placing an AI firewall in front of LLM applications for request scanning, rate limiting, sensitive-data detection, and planned prompt validation. It is vendor design context, not independent comparative effectiveness evidence.

verifier_provenance.scope_note: Context only; the page explicitly described prompt validation as under development.

sources.title: How Not To Sort By Average Rating
sources.content: Evan Miller's 2009 article demonstrates why raw differences and raw averages mis-rank small samples and recommends the lower bound of a Wilson score interval for binary ratings. It is useful calibration context, not a validation of the platform's future reputation metric.

verifier_provenance.scope_note: Contextual method source; downstream metric choice still requires ticket-specific calibration evidence.

sources.title: A Survey of AI Agent Protocols
sources.content: The arXiv record dated 2025-04-23 identifies a multi-author survey that classifies and compares AI agent protocols. It is a protocol-landscape source, not an official specification for any individual protocol.

sources.title: Beyond Message Passing: Toward Semantically Aligned Agent Communication
sources.content: The current arXiv metadata dated 2026-03-30 identifies a 14-author study of 18 protocols. Its abstract reports mature transport and syntax mechanisms but limited semantic alignment and verification mechanisms.

verifier_provenance.correction_note: The historical local title beginning 'A Semantic View' is retained as provenance; current arXiv metadata uses 'Beyond Message Passing: Toward Semantically Aligned Agent Communication'.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026
sources.content: The official OWASP page dated 2025-12-09 presents a community-reviewed risk framework for agentic applications. It is a Z-tail spot check and shares the OWASP independence group with I1 and I2.

claims.text: The bounded S1-001 queue contains 12 decision-relevant canonical records, including three tail spot checks (SV2, SV3, and Z13), and does not claim verification of the remaining historical u population.
Doyle, Dung, and Prakken/Sartor provide three distinct canonical works for reason maintenance, abstract argument acceptability, and defeasible priorities.
The scoped security set contains an OWASP threat-taxonomy group, an independent Cloudflare gateway design note, and an independent in-toto supply-chain provenance standard.
SV2 and SV3 are distinct protocol-landscape studies; SV3's current metadata reports 18 protocols and a gap between mature transport/syntax and limited semantic alignment or verification.
PROV-O and in-toto are independent canonical sources for attribution/delegation vocabulary and ordered software supply-chain provenance respectively.
A promotion decision should count unique canonical_source_id and independence_group pairs, never hostnames, mirrors, or publisher labels alone.
Vendor architecture notes and practitioner methods can be verified as context class c while remaining inadmissible as sole support for a high-risk platform claim.
The historical registry count of 176 u entries is treated as an input assumption outside this targeted run; S1-001 does not mutate or exhaustively re-verify that registry.
Adopt an append-only, claim-scoped promotion queue with explicit status, provenance, independence, contradiction, and expiry fields for later Stage 1 tickets.

research_plan.content:
# Research question
What targeted verification and promotion policy is sufficient for decision-critical u sources without implying that all 176 historical u records were verified?

# Method
Freeze a 12-record queue derived from downstream Stage 1 decisions; review canonical publisher or author pages; record canonical_source_id, publisher_id, independence_group, original status, proposed status, verifier, method, and corrections; test mirror/Sybil and missing-provenance near misses.

# Scope
F8, F16, F18, F19, I1, I2, I8, I14, J13, SV2, SV3, and Z13. Three tail records are explicitly covered.

# Non-scope
No live retrieval adapter is added, no historical registry row is edited in place, and the remaining u population is not asserted verified.

# Stop rule
Block a promotion if identity is ambiguous, fewer than two independent canonical groups support a high-risk claim, or the queue expands into mass verification.

source_registry.content:
# Status policy
- v: canonical or primary source verified for the exact scoped claim, with dated verifier provenance.
- c: verified context or contradiction source; not sufficient alone for a high-risk claim.
- u: unresolved or missing verifier provenance; remains unpromoted.
- x: identity/content invalid or unavailable for the scoped claim.
- x-excluded: deliberately outside scope, with an explicit exclusion rationale.

Harness-level verification_status=verified means this run verified the record and its provenance. Policy-level promotion_decision=v or c is stored separately, so c is not silently upgraded to v.

# Queue
| ID | Original | Proposed | Publisher | Independence group | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F8 | u | v | w3c | w3c-prov-working-group | canonical provenance standard |
| F16 | u | v | elsevier-artificial-intelligence | doyle-tms | corrected DOI preserved |
| F18 | u | v | elsevier-artificial-intelligence | dung-argumentation-framework | distinct canonical work |
| F19 | u | v | taylor-francis-jancl | prakken-sartor-defeasible-priorities | journal/DOI correction preserved |
| I1 | u | v | owasp-genai | owasp-genai-taxonomy | dated 2025 baseline |
| I2 | u | v | owasp-genai | owasp-genai-taxonomy | same group as I1/Z13 |
| I8 | u | v | cncf-in-toto | cncf-in-toto | independent supply-chain standard |
| I14 | u | c | cloudflare | cloudflare-vendor | vendor design context only |
| J13 | u | c | evan-miller | evan-miller-rating-method | calibration context only |
| SV2 | u | v | arxiv | sv2-author-group | tail spot check |
| SV3 | u | v | arxiv | sv3-author-group | tail spot check and title correction |
| Z13 | u | v | owasp-genai | owasp-genai-taxonomy | tail spot check |

# Independence
Different URLs or publisher labels do not create independence. Mirrors inherit the canonical source's group. Multiple OWASP pages add coverage but count once for independence. Shared publisher alone does not collapse distinct canonical author works, but the grouping rationale must be recorded.

feature_catalog.content:
# Downstream enablement
The promotion queue is an evidence-control feature used before later tickets cite a source. Knowledge-gate work consumes F16/F18/F19; provenance and lineage work consumes F8/I8; security work consumes I1/I2/I14/Z13; protocol work consumes SV2/SV3; calibration work may use J13 only as context.

# Required fields
Every queue item carries claim_scope, original_status, proposed_status, canonical_source_id, canonical_uri, publisher_id, independence_group, verifier, verification_method, verified_at, correction_note, contradiction_refs, and expiry_or_refresh_rule.

# Exclusions
The feature does not fetch pages, infer independence from domains, or promote a source merely because metadata looks plausible.

architecture_models.content:
# Control flow
Historical registry (append-only input) -> bounded candidate queue -> identity resolution -> provenance verification -> independence grouping -> claim-specific decision v/c/u/x/x-excluded -> immutable decision event -> downstream admissibility query.

# Authority boundary
The verifier proposes evidence; a policy gate computes admissibility. Retrieved text is untrusted and cannot alter thresholds, status vocabulary, scope, or capabilities. A correction creates a new decision event linked to the erroneous prior value.

# Storage boundary
Canonical state belongs in the AgentOS DB and evidence pack. Obsidian is a deterministic readable projection. The DeepeekHarness historical registry remains unchanged by this ticket.

mental_model.content:
# Human-readable decision card
Show the exact claim, current status, original status, canonical identity, independent groups, corroborators, contradiction/context sources, corrections, verifier/method/date, and why the threshold passed or failed.

# Avoid misleading signals
Do not display a raw URL count as source diversity. Group OWASP-family records together, label vendor notes as c, and visibly retain F16/F19 metadata corrections. Use '12 targeted records reviewed' rather than '176 sources verified'.

# Operator actions
An operator can approve the bounded queue, request another independent group, downgrade to c/u, exclude with rationale, or stop on ambiguous identity.

ontology.content:
# Classes
SourceRecord, CanonicalSource, Publisher, IndependenceGroup, ClaimScope, VerificationEvent, PromotionDecision, CorrectionEvent, MirrorRelation, ContradictionRelation, and ExclusionDecision.

# Status semantics
v and c are positive but non-equivalent policy decisions; u is unresolved; x is unusable for the scoped claim; x-excluded is intentionally out of scope. Harness verified is evidence about the verification event, not an alias for policy v.

# Relations
SourceRecord identifies CanonicalSource; CanonicalSource publishedBy Publisher; CanonicalSource memberOf IndependenceGroup; VerificationEvent evaluatedFor ClaimScope; PromotionDecision basedOn VerificationEvent; MirrorRelation inheritsCanonicalIdentity; CorrectionEvent supersedes but never erases the prior assertion.

# Invariants
Every promotion candidate has exactly one canonical_source_id, publisher_id, and independence_group. A mirror cannot introduce a new independence group. Every v/c decision has dated verifier provenance.

mathematical_model.content:
# Admission rule
For candidate source s and claim q, admissible_v(s,q)=1 only when identity_resolved=1, provenance_complete=1, primary_or_canonical=1, and no blocking contradiction exists. Context-only evidence yields c, not v.

# High-risk claim support
Let G(q) be unique independence groups among admissible supporters and N(q) be distinct canonical sources. Promotion of a high-risk claim requires |G(q)| >= 2 and N(q) >= 3, where the third item may be context or contradiction evidence. URL count is never used.

# Mirror probe
If m mirrors s, canonical_source_id(m)=canonical_source_id(s) and independence_group(m)=independence_group(s); therefore adding m changes neither |G(q)| nor N(q). Expected delta is 0.

# Queue bounds
This run has 12 candidates and 3 tail spot checks. Coverage is 12/12 for the frozen queue and explicitly not 176/176 for the historical u population.

# Refresh
A decision expires or is rechecked when canonical identity changes, a contradiction arrives, a downstream claim expands, or its ticket-defined freshness interval elapses.

synthesis_and_gaps.content:
# Result
Adopt the bounded promotion policy. Ten queue records qualify as scoped v and two vendor/practitioner records (I14, J13) qualify as c. The decision is claim-specific and does not rewrite the historical source registry.

# Corrections
F16's earlier DOI was a plausible near-miss; the correct DOI ends 90008-0. F19's earlier journal/DOI attribution was wrong; the canonical record is Journal of Applied Non-Classical Logics with DOI 10.1080/11663081.1997.10510900. SV3's current arXiv title differs from the historical local title. All three corrections retain the earlier value as error provenance.

# Gaps
No external human auditor participated in this run. Source content was reviewed at canonical pages and metadata level, not reproduced or archived in full. Availability and freshness can change. The remaining historical u population is deliberately unresolved.

# Next actions
Implement the queue schema and exact independence gate before downstream tickets consume promotions; obtain external audit when S1-020 closes the portfolio; refresh any source when its downstream claim changes.

independent_audit.content:
# Adversarial review
The verifier pass treated every promotion as suspect and recomputed the queue from source identity, publisher, independence group, and dated provenance. It found no claim that all 176 historical u records were verified.

# Probe 1: mirror/Sybil
A synthetic mirror with a different host and publisher label but the same canonical_source_id and independence_group produced delta |G|=0 and delta N=0. PASS: it cannot satisfy the threshold. The three OWASP records likewise count as one independence group.

# Probe 2: plausible metadata without provenance
A plausible u title with no verifier or method remains u. F16's wrong DOI and F19's wrong venue/DOI were not silently accepted; corrected identities are new scoped decisions with the old values preserved in correction_note. PASS.

# Coverage checks
All 12 frozen candidates contain canonical_source_id, publisher_id, and independence_group; SV2, SV3, and Z13 cover the required tail spot checks; all five policy status classes are defined. High-risk evidence clusters have at least three sources and at least two independent canonical groups.

# Verdict
PASS_WITH_LIMITS. The audit role is distinct from the subject producer and used an adversarial pass, but it is not an external human or independently operated model. Portfolio closure must preserve that limit and may request external confirmation.

platform_plan.content:
# Scope
Implement only the promotion queue, append-only decision records, exact independence computation, and downstream admissibility query. Do not add retrieval adapters or mass-verify the historical registry.

# Architecture
Add canonical SourceIdentity, VerificationEvent, PromotionDecision, and CorrectionEvent records to canonical storage. The gate owns status transitions; retrieved documents remain untrusted inputs. Wiki pages are projections with links to claims, sources, decisions, and corrections.

# Workstreams
1. Schema and migration for claim-scoped status and provenance. 2. Canonicalization and mirror grouping. 3. Deterministic v/c/u/x/x-excluded gate. 4. Queue UI/wiki projection. 5. Regression fixtures for DOI/title corrections and Sybil mirrors. 6. Downstream query API.

# Milestones
M1 freezes the field contract and fixtures. M2 persists append-only decisions and corrections. M3 enforces independence and status gates. M4 emits evidence pack/wiki links. M5 integrates S1-009 through S1-012 consumers after their dependencies pass.

# Verification
Require 12/12 queue-field completeness, exact grouping for OWASP and mirrors, both adversarial probes green, no historical-registry mutation, evidence-pack v3 with fresh chain/latest evaluation, and wiki-check ok=true. High-risk claims require at least three canonical sources across at least two independence groups.

# Risks
Publisher consolidation can look like dependence; authorship overlap may be missed; vendor pages can change; a verified record can be over-generalized beyond its claim scope; an operator may confuse harness verified with policy v. Mitigate with explicit scope, grouping rationale, content hashes, corrections, and expiry.

# Open decisions
Choose the refresh interval per source class; decide whether S1-020 requires an external human auditor; define acceptable canonical archive snapshots; decide how later tickets request a promotion without changing this frozen queue.

progress.content:
# 2026-08-24
Status: ready for harness evaluation. Frozen queue: 12/12 candidates authored. Tail checks: SV2, SV3, Z13. Live canonical/primary review completed for the scoped records.

Corrections discovered: F16 DOI near-miss, F19 venue/DOI mismatch, and SV3 title drift; prior values preserved in provenance. Probe definitions and expected outcomes recorded.

Declared limits: no mass verification of 176 historical u entries; no external human auditor; no live retrieval adapter; no production or Goal ACCEPTED claim. Next event is the canonical research-plan evaluation and post-run wiki check.

limitations: The auditor role is process-separated and adversarial but is not an external human or independently operated model.
The run verifies the frozen 12-record queue only; it does not verify all 176 historical u records.
Canonical pages and metadata were reviewed live, but full third-party content was not archived in this repository.
